graph.name: Replace a repeated phrase
graph.description:
Replace known habitual wording with an explicit literal rule and no model call.

Lesson: Draft Text Rules makes exact literal replacements without a model; scope and protected literals bound the change, with explicit review afterward.

Limitations: Configured literal replacement does not detect semantic repetition or judge whether the replacement reads well.

Opening installs an unassigned copy. Bind local model roles and provide the documented evidence before running.

Post: at most 0 auxiliary calls. Preview before publishing or applying.

Try changing:
Change replacement to breathed out and compare the fixed phrase in context.
Protect the complete configured phrase and verify no replacement is proposed.

Documentation specimen (does not seed chat or actor memory):

Before: He let out a breath he didn't know he was holding, then opened the letter.

After: He exhaled, then opened the letter.

First editable rule: reply → rules → validate → review → apply. All deterministic; no model profile. Rule JSON explicitly chooses literal kind, pattern, replacement and empty flags.

Literal limits: whole permits matching in narration/dialogue, excluding protected literals. Only configured wording changes; semantic repetition detection and context-sensitive repairs belong to later lessons.

Letter-opening phrase · snapshot (reply)
Purpose: Freeze the latest completed text-only breath-phrase reply.
Fixture: He let out a breath he didn't know he was holding, then opened the letter. "No more delays," Mira said.
Inspect: Confirm exact phrase and exhale-before-letter chronology.

One literal breath replacement (rules)
Purpose: Replace an approved habitual phrase deterministically.
Inspect: Expected He exhaled, then opened the letter.; exact case-sensitive matching. No match means no change.

Check the fixed-phrase boundary (validate)
Purpose: Validate literal changes against the frozen source.
Inspect: Check original surrounding text and protected Mira/No more delays.

Review exhale and chronology (review)
Purpose: Require approval of the fixed wording choice.
Inspect: Exhaling still precedes opening; reject if the phrase was intentional.

Offer the literal phrase repair (apply)
Purpose: Offer the zero-call repair candidate.
Inspect: Full root Host result: compare the phrase, then Apply or Reject.
